# bugs #3979: Of several designated initializers for an anonymous struct in a union, only one is applied

- Ticket: https://sourceforge.net/p/sdcc/bugs/3979/
- Category: [Fixes that need a decision](../../fix-decision.md)
- Evidence: tested on r17193
- Recommended action: Confirm the two choices under Decision. Apply after the patch for #3393 and close. Related lists the faults that stay.
- Patch: [bugs-3979.patch](../../patches/bugs-3979.patch), commit [`11fa673de`](https://github.com/mdmower/sdcc/commit/11fa673ded02bafe5c49d424321983f77b6b26f5). Apply after `bugs-4157-1.patch`, `bugs-3121.patch`, `bugs-2948.patch`, `bugs-3847.patch`, `bugs-3393.patch`.
<!-- end of generated block -->

## Finding

`union u { unsigned int raw; struct { unsigned char lo, hi; }; }` of the last comment takes one of
the two initializers in `{.lo = 0x34, .hi = 0x12}`. The attached `main.c` was compiled with
`sdcc -mmcs51 main.c` on r17192 with the earlier patches of this report and run in ucsim. The two
bytes are `34 00`, and `34 12` is expected. Three kinds of objects lose initializers.

- A union with an anonymous struct as a later alternative, such as `union u`. One designated
  member gets its value, in the data image and when code initializes the object. Where the
  compiler emits the object as a data image, it gives warning 147.
- A union that starts with an anonymous struct, as in the description. `B`, `C`, and `D` lose
  their initializers when code initializes the object, which is the case for automatic objects
  and for file-scope objects in the small model.
- A struct with an anonymous union, as in the first comment. In the data image, one of several
  designated members of an anonymous struct in that union gets its value.

With the earlier patches of this report, the constant of the description and `Foo1` to `Foo3` of
the first comment have the correct bytes.

## Cause

`promoteAnonStructs` in `src/SDCCsymt.c` replaces an anonymous struct by its members in the member
list of the union. `printIvalStruct` in `src/SDCCglue.c` emits one member of the alternative that
a designator names. `createIvalStruct` in `src/SDCCast.c` leaves its loop over the designated
initializers after the first one when the type is a union.

## Fix

`promoteAnonStructs` sets the new flag `anonaltstart` for the first member of each alternative of
a union except the first alternative. The new `differentAlternatives` in `src/SDCCsymt.c` tells
from this flag and from the marks of the patch for #2948 whether two members are in different
alternatives of a union. `printIvalStruct` emits each member of the alternative that has an
initializer. `createIvalStruct` applies each of the designated initializers that the list of a
union starts with. When they name members of the first alternative, the members after them take
the initializers without a designator, and the other members of an automatic object are set to
zero.

## Decision

For three kinds of lists, both functions use one initializer of the alternative, as they do
without the patch.

- Lists with initializers for members of two alternatives of one union.
- Lists in which an initializer without a designator follows a designator and C assigns it to a
  member of a later alternative. `nextInitSlot` in `src/SDCCval.c` does not assign it to that
  member. `unbraceAnonInit` marks these lists with the new member `inexact` of `initList`.
- When code initializes a union, lists in which initializers without a designator follow the
  designators and the last designator does not name the last of the designated members.
  `{.c = 3, .a = 1, 2}` for `union q` of the test sets `c` alone, and C also sets `a` and `b`.

The other choice is to apply every designated initializer that a list has for the members of one
alternative. It corrects more lists, and it makes lists wrong that are right without the patch.
One of them is `const union n cn1 = {.d = 5, .b = 1, 0, 0};` of the test. C gives `01 00 00`,
because the first 0 is for `c` and replaces the initializer of `d`. With and without the patch the
compiler emits `b` alone. With the other choice it emits `01 05 00`. When code initializes an
object with this list, the bytes are `00 05 00` with and without the patch.

The patch also changes where warning 147 appears. When code initializes a union, an initializer in
excess after a designator for a member of the first alternative gets the warning, as in
`union { int a; char b; } x = {.a = 1, 5};`. Without the patch the compiler discards the 5 without
a diagnostic. The initializers that the patch emits in a data image do not get the warning.

## Verification

`support/regression/tests/bug-3979.c` has 29 assertions for constant, file-scope, and automatic
objects. The patch was tested on r17192 with the patches of this report up to the one for #3393.
Without the source change, 16 assertions fail on each of the six mcs51 variants, on stm8, and on
ucz80. With it the test passes on these and on host. The regression suite has 0 failures for
host, the six mcs51 variants, stm8, and ucz80, and the diagnostics suite has 0 failures for mcs51,
mcs51-large, mcs51-stack-auto, z80, and stm8. For mcs51-small, mcs51-large, stm8, and ucz80, the
assembly of the other regression tests is identical with and without the patch.

210 initializer lists were compiled for mcs51 as a constant, a file-scope, and an automatic
object, with the small and the large model, and the 1260 objects were compared with GCC's result.
670 are right with and without the patch, 175 are right with the patch only, and 415 are wrong
with and without it. In three more sets with 944 lists, the patch corrects 366 objects. The images
of 17600 more constant objects were compared with GCC's bytes, and the patch corrects 198 of them.
In every set, each object that is right without the patch is right with it.

## Related

These faults are present with and without the patch.

- An initializer without a designator after a designator for a member of a later alternative is
  dropped or assigned to the member after the union. `{.lo = 0x34, 0x12}` for `union u` gives
  `34 00`, and C gives `34 12`. The mark `inexact` is for the whole list of a struct, so a second
  union in that struct also gets one initializer.
- When designators name members of two alternatives, the result does not follow the order of the
  list. `{.d = 1, .b = 2}` for `struct s` of the test gives `00 01 00 00 00`, and C gives
  `00 02 00 00 00`.
- Bit-fields in an alternative other than the first get wrong data or none. `{.b1 = 3}` for a
  union of `unsigned char raw` and `struct { unsigned char b0 : 1, b1 : 3, b2 : 4; }` gives `03`
  in the data image, and C gives `06`.
- In the shape of #3393, the data image lacks several designated members of one alternative. The
  entry for #3393 has `{.a = 1, .s = 7, .t = 9, .z = 4}` for `struct W` as the example.
- In an automatic object, `{1, .b = 3}` for
  `struct { char p; union { int i; struct { char a, b, c; }; }; char q; }` leaves `a` without a
  store.
- When code initializes a union and the first designator names a member of a later alternative of
  a union in it, the compiler drops the initializers without a designator and does not give a
  diagnostic. `{.y1 = 1, .y2 = 2, 3}` for a union of
  `struct { char p; union { char x; struct { char y1, y2; }; }; char z; }` and `long l` gives
  `00 01 02 00`, and C gives `00 01 02 03`.
- In an automatic union, the bytes that the first alternative does not cover and the bits of
  unnamed bit-fields keep their content. GCC sets them to zero.
